title: Node.js 22.18 breaks CI tests after experimental type stripping becomes enabled by default
body: After updating from Node.js 22.17 to 22.18, our builds consistently fail on Linux, Windows, and Azure DevOps agents. The code works again only if we add `--no-experimental-strip-types` to the Node.js command line. I would not expect a minor release of an existing LTS line to enable an experimental feature by default when it breaks existing projects.

symptoms_visible: CI builds consistently fail with Node.js 22.18 after working with 22.17; adding `--no-experimental-strip-types` makes them run again.
N0.label: N0 Node 22.18 CI failure reported

symptoms_visible: Under Node.js 22.18, tests report that `__dirname` is not defined even though the package has no `type` field and previously behaved as CommonJS; disabling type stripping avoids the failure.
N1.label: N1 exact failure and module expectation collected

symptoms_visible: The project still fails on Node.js 22.18 without the opt-out flag, and it is running its tests with Mocha 10.
N2.label: N2 Mocha 10 compatibility cause isolated

symptoms_visible: The failure remains after testing a revert of the suspected `.js` handler change.
N2_x.label: N2_x handler-revert aftermath

symptoms_visible: With the latest Mocha, the original tests run successfully on Node.js 22.18 without `--no-experimental-strip-types`.
N3.label: N3 Mocha upgrade verified

symptoms_visible: The project uses the updated Mocha release, and its CI tests pass on Node.js 22.18 without disabling experimental type stripping.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with Mocha upgrade

question_patterns: What exact error do the failing builds produce?
Can you share the error or stack trace seen on Node.js 22.18?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The immediate error I saw was that `__dirname` was suddenly not defined.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The process exits before loading our tests because Node itself cannot start, and there is no module-loading or `__dirname` error.
The same failure says `require is not defined` instead of `__dirname is not defined`.

question_patterns: Does the package declare a module type in package.json?
Is this project expected to run as CommonJS or ESM?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We do not specify `type` in our package.json files, so the project was expected to fall back to CommonJS as it did through Node.js 22.17.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every package explicitly declares `"type": "module"`, and the code intentionally runs as ESM.

question_patterns: Does the same behavior occur on Node.js 24?
Have you tried another Node release with and without the type-stripping flag?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I had also struggled with the latest Node.js 24.5.0, and `--no-experimental-strip-types` solves those problems too.

edges.comment: Reporter supplied the concrete `__dirname` symptom, the lack of a package `type` field, and confirmation that the opt-out also changes behavior on Node.js 24.

question_patterns: Which test framework and version does the affected project use?
Are Mocha or custom TypeScript registration hooks involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found that our project uses Mocha 10.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing command does not use Mocha or any custom TypeScript loader; it is a plain `node app.js` invocation.
The project uses a different Mocha 10 patch release.

question_patterns: Can you provide a minimal reproduction showing the test runner and TypeScript hook?
Can this be reproduced with Mocha and `ts-node/register` outside the large project?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A minimal reproduction from another affected participant uses Mocha 10 with `mocha --require ts-node/register`; it fails after type stripping becomes active, while a test using tsx did not show that particular reproduction.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimal reproduction also fails on Node.js 22.17 and succeeds on 22.18, the reverse of the reported behavior.
The reproduction repository uses a different CI provider.

edges.comment: The minimal Mocha 10 and ts-node reproduction came from another affected participant and is folded into the simulated user side. Engineer analysis inferred that Node now throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX` where Mocha 10 expected `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION`; Mocha 10 misses its fallback, while Mocha 11 tries `require()` first so the registered TypeScript hook runs.

solution.intent: Revert the suspected Node.js `.js` handler change from PR 58657 on the assumption that it caused the loader incompatibility.
solution.concrete_example: Build Node.js with PR 58657 reverted and rerun the affected loader reproduction.

edges.comment: The thread records an actual test reverting PR 58657; the issue persisted. The investigation instead pointed to loaders receiving the new `module-typescript` and `commonjs-typescript` formats and, for the reporter's Mocha 10 case, changed error/fallback behavior.

question_patterns: Can you upgrade from Mocha 10 to the latest Mocha and rerun without `--no-experimental-strip-types`?
Please test whether Mocha 11 fixes the original project without the Node opt-out flag.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Upgrading to the latest Mocha fixes the initial problem. I no longer have to specify `--no-experimental-strip-types`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest Mocha produces the same `__dirname` failure unless type stripping is disabled.
The upgrade fixes the tests on both Linux and Windows, but the CI job needs its lockfile refreshed before using the new version.

edges.comment: This is a handler-initiated dependency-version probe, so it is modeled as clarification only. The reporter explicitly verified that current Mocha fixes the original failure without the Node flag.

solution.intent: Resolve the reporter's project by adopting the latest Mocha release, whose module-loading order is compatible with Node.js 22.18 type stripping, rather than permanently disabling the Node feature.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade the project from Mocha 10 to the latest Mocha 11 release, refresh the lockfile, and run CI on Node.js 22.18 without `NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-strip-types`; keep the opt-out only as a temporary workaround for dependency combinations that have not yet been updated.

edges.comment: Reporter-specific resolution from c15-c20: the Node change exposed Mocha 10's loader fallback assumption, and the reporter confirmed that upgrading Mocha resolves the initial project without disabling type stripping. Later reports involving tsx, swc, ts-node loaders, Jest, or node:test are distinct dependency combinations and do not invalidate this reporter's verified resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the reporter-specific root cause: Node.js 22.18 enabling type stripping changed TypeScript module-loading behavior and the error from an attempted import, while the project's Mocha 10 fallback logic did not recognize the new `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX` path; current Mocha tries `require()` first so the registered TypeScript hook can handle the file.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the failure starts on Node.js 22.18, disappears with `--no-experimental-strip-types`, the project uses Mocha 10, and upgrading to the latest Mocha fixes the original problem without that flag.
Must not recommend reverting PR 58657 as the resolution, because that revert was tested and the issue persisted.

Must distinguish the reporter's verified Mocha 10 issue from later reports involving different combinations such as latest Mocha with custom ts-node loaders, tsx, swc, Jest, or node:test; those may require their own reproductions or dependency patches.

Must treat `--no-experimental-strip-types` as a temporary workaround rather than the final reporter-specific fix, and must not declare resolution until the upgraded Mocha setup is verified in CI on Node.js 22.18 without the flag.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced application maintainer working on a large, seven-year-old Node.js project. Comfortable managing Node versions, CI options, package dependencies, and testing upgrades, but initially lacks a small isolated reproduction.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and practical. Reports version boundaries and workarounds clearly, questions LTS compatibility policy, cooperates with requests for more detail, and confirms when a dependency upgrade fixes the original issue.
